key_insight: The paper shows that sentiment-augmented deep reinforcement learning, especially DDPG, can outperform buy-and-hold in active trading when trained with an alpha-based reward and robust validation.
engineering_relevance: It demonstrates a practical pipeline for finance agents that combines news sentiment, technical indicators, and hyperparameter search to produce daily long/flat/short decisions under realistic market constraints.
method: Formulate trading as a discrete-action MDP with daily long, flat, or short actions.
Fuse technical indicators, cyclical calendar features, and LLaMA 3.2 news sentiment scores.
Train and compare PG, PPO, DQL, and DDPG with alpha reward, randomized episode starts, and Ray Tune optimization.
evidence_signal: On the CLEF FinMMEval Task 3 test set, DDPG achieved 54.96% cumulative return for TSLA and 1.58% for BTC, while DQL was chosen for the live endpoint based on the best validation Sharpe ratio.
watch_item: The large validation-to-test gap suggests the learned policy may not transfer reliably across regime changes, especially from bull-market validation to bear-market test periods.
paper_title: CLaC@FinMMEval 2026 Task 3: Sentiment-Augmented Deep Reinforcement Learning for Active Trading -- An Alpha-Reward Approach
